clue.text: They should correct faulty hearing

parts.note: a hearing here is a legal trial, not the sense of the ears; bodies that review flawed trials are the reading

explanation.surface: A description of hearing aids or ear specialists who fix poor hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hearing' tempts you towards ears and deafness, but it means a case heard in court, and these higher tribunals put right a flawed verdict.
explanation.definitionFit: Higher tribunals review lower verdicts and overturn mistaken rulings, which is correcting a faulty trial.

clue.text: A vote on the island can be assumed

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece written on top of another comes before it

parts.note: a cross, X, is the mark put on a ballot paper as a vote
IOM is the abbreviation for the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: A ballot held on an island whose outcome everyone takes for granted.
explanation.walkthrough: IOM is the Isle of Man, a self-governing island in the Irish Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-evident principle is something taken as true without proof.

clue.text: Pulse protectors

parts.note: pulses are edible seeds such as peas and lentils, and the reading is the cases that shield them as they grow

explanation.surface: It sounds like medical gear guarding a heartbeat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pulse' reads as a heartbeat, but here it is the food sense: peas, beans and lentils.
explanation.definitionFit: The green shells of a legume plant enclose and shelter the seeds until harvest.

clue.text: Troublemakers might give you the shakes?

definitions.meaning: people who stir up unrest or protest
read literally, things that stir or shake, like mixing machines

explanation.surface: Rabble-rousers so alarming they could make you tremble.
explanation.definitionFit: Activists who stir up dissent are rabble-rousers, and machines that agitate liquids literally shake things.

clue.text: See 1
Love to be different — so typical of the female

parts.note: love is nil in tennis scoring, shaped like the letter O
to vary is to be different or change

explanation.surface: A remark that loving variety is a typically feminine trait.
explanation.walkthrough: O for love comes from tennis, where a zero score is called love.
explanation.definitionFit: The egg-producing organ is found only in a woman or other female animal, so it characterises the sex.

clue.text: Shiny new recruit leads team of high flyers

definitions.text: Shiny new recruit leads team of high flyers

parts.words: Shiny new recruit leads team of high flyers
parts.note: the high flyers are Santa's airborne reindeer, and the shiny newcomer with a glowing nose went to the front of the sleigh team

explanation.surface: A bright new hire is put in charge of a team of top achievers.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Christmas song the red-nosed reindeer, mocked at first, is chosen to lead the sleigh on a foggy night; 'shiny' is his glowing nose.
explanation.definitionFit: The song's latecomer reindeer has a gleaming red nose and was picked to guide the flying team.

clue.text: Newspaper type gets lover into bed? On the contrary!

indicators.note: the surface puts the lover inside the bed, the container order the clue then turns round
this reverses the stated order, so the bed goes inside the lover rather than the lover inside the bed

parts.note: a suitor is a man courting someone, a lover
taken as written

explanation.surface: A journalist takes a lover to bed, or perhaps the other way round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the contrary' flips 'gets lover into bed': BED goes into SUITOR instead, giving SU-BED-ITOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A desk journalist who checks and corrects copy before printing is a kind of newspaper worker.

clue.text: Really huge, it turns brown in colour initially

indicators.note: turns tells us the little word it is flipped to run the other way

parts.note: tan is a light brown colour

indicators.note: initially means take the opening letters of in and colour

explanation.surface: Something enormous that changes colour to brown.
explanation.definitionFit: Gigantic, like the mythical giants of Greek legend, means extraordinarily large.

clue.text: Terrible score, you wouldn't credit it!

parts.note: bad means terrible or poor
a score is something owed, as in settling a score, so a debt

explanation.surface: A dismal result in a game that is hard to believe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'You wouldn't credit it' looks like an exclamation of disbelief, but in accounting it is a loan never repaid, which a lender will not count as an asset.
explanation.definitionFit: An unrecoverable loan is written off rather than counted as money due, so no accountant would give credit for it.

clue.text: Remarkable chap, a flag waver once

parts.note: signal as an adjective means notable or remarkable, as in a signal achievement
a man is a chap

explanation.surface: A tribute to an outstanding fellow who once waved a flag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Signal' as an adjective (a signal honour) means striking; the definition is a railway worker who once used flags to direct trains.
explanation.definitionFit: Railway workers formerly controlled trains with hand flags and levers from a trackside box.

clue.text: Everlasting life has no time for sin

indicators.note: has no means the following item is taken away from the longer word

parts.note: everlasting life is the state of never dying, immortality

explanation.surface: Eternal life leaves no room for wrongdoing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Has no' removes T from IMMORTALITY, leaving the word for wickedness.
explanation.definitionFit: Wickedness or wrongful conduct, behaviour against moral law, is a broad synonym for sin.

clue.text: Pound to join superior party game

parts.note: L, from Latin libra, is the abbreviation for a pound
U means upper-class or superior in British usage
a do is a party or celebration

explanation.surface: Someone is urged to spend a pound and join an upmarket party game.
explanation.walkthrough: U for superior is British slang for upper-class, as opposed to non-U.
explanation.definitionFit: A simple board game for children, played with dice and counters, is a classic pastime.

clue.text: Some bring us together to show enthusiasm

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A plea to unite people so they display keenness.
explanation.definitionFit: Hearty relish or zest is the eagerness one shows when keen.

clue.text: Top troops possibly armed with guns

definitions.text: Top troops possibly armed with guns

parts.words: Top troops possibly armed with guns
parts.note: the top troops are the elite Guards regiments, and one of their soldiers carries a rifle

explanation.surface: Elite soldiers who may well be carrying firearms.
explanation.walkthrough: The Guards are Britain's elite household regiments, famous for ceremonial duty at royal palaces; a soldier serving in them is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A soldier of the Guards, the elite household regiments, belongs to the top troops and carries weapons.

clue.text: One prepared to box, say, is just a beginner

indicators.note: prepared means the letters of One are made ready in a fresh order
say signals that the next part is a word as spoken rather than as spelt

parts.note: to box is to fight with fists

explanation.surface: Someone willing to take up boxing is only a novice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prepared' rearranges ONE into NEO; 'say' gives PHYTE, which is said like FIGHT, the meaning of 'to box'.
explanation.definitionFit: A novice or new convert is someone just starting out.

clue.text: Old transport anthologies

definitions.meaning: horse-drawn or early public passenger vehicles
volumes collecting several works in one book

explanation.surface: Vintage vehicles alongside collected volumes.
explanation.definitionFit: The full Latin form of buses names old public vehicles, and the word also means single volumes collecting several works.

clue.text: Musical party with plenty of drink left

parts.note: to carouse is to drink heavily and make merry

explanation.surface: A show tune at a boozy party where drink is still left over.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the Rodgers and Hammerstein stage show, not the fairground ride.
explanation.definitionFit: A Rodgers and Hammerstein stage show of 1945 bears this title, so it is an example of a musical.

clue.text: Ham is gone, cat looks suspect

parts.note: over means finished or gone

indicators.note: looks suspect says the letters of cat are dodgy and need rearranging

explanation.surface: Ham has vanished and the cat looks guilty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ham' looks like the meat the cat stole, but it is a verb: to perform too theatrically.
explanation.definitionFit: To ham is to perform in an exaggerated theatrical way.

clue.text: Better check back with head cashier

indicators.note: with here means holding the extra letter inside the reversed word
back says the word for check is written in reverse

parts.note: to rein is to check or restrain

indicators.note: head means the first letter of cashier

explanation.surface: A recommendation to verify things with the chief cashier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' turns REIN into NIER, and C from 'head cashier' goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: More pleasant or agreeable is a comparative of good, so it means better.

clue.text: Halve cost? It's usual to live together

indicators.note: halve tells us to keep only the first half of the word cost

parts.note: a habit is what one usually does

explanation.surface: Couples ask whether halving costs is normal when they share a home.
explanation.definitionFit: To share a home as a couple without being married is a common meaning.

clue.text: Cutting tool joins on, so to speak

indicators.note: so to speak means the word is heard rather than written

parts.note: adds means joins on, attaches

explanation.surface: A tool that attaches things, as it were.
explanation.definitionFit: A woodworker's blade set at right angles to the handle shapes timber by chopping.

clue.text: Remain bottom like naughty boys may do in class

definitions.text: like naughty boys may do in class

parts.note: to stay is to remain
behind is a word for the backside, the bottom

explanation.surface: Unruly schoolboys kept back after the lesson, sitting at the foot of the class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottom' suggests coming last in class, but it is the backside; the definition describes being kept in for detention.
explanation.definitionFit: Pupils kept in after lessons for detention are made to remain when others leave.

clue.text: Crack uses up most of glue, for instance

indicators.note: uses up most of says only part of the word survives, its last letters removed

parts.note: glue is an example of a solvent, a substance that dissolves others

explanation.surface: Breakage repair that exhausts nearly all the adhesive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uses up most of' drops NT from the end of SOLVENT.
explanation.definitionFit: To crack a puzzle or code is to work it out.

clue.text: Bottle that's never broken

indicators.note: broken means the letters of never are smashed and rearranged

explanation.surface: A bottle that has never been smashed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottle' is British slang for courage, not a container.
explanation.definitionFit: Courage or daring is what both words mean in informal British English.

clue.text: Friendly question concerning my proficiency

definitions.meaning: split into three words it asks whether I am capable

explanation.surface: Someone sociably asks whether they are good enough.
explanation.definitionFit: Good-natured and amiable people are friendly, and split into three words the letters ask whether I can do something.

clue.text: One's love prevents possible signs of depression

parts.note: one is I and the possessive gives I'S, written IS
love is nil in tennis, shaped like O
bars means prevents or blocks

explanation.surface: A love-sick person stops showing signs of being low.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Depression' is a low-pressure weather system, not low mood; the lines on a weather map show it.
explanation.definitionFit: Lines joining points of equal pressure on a weather chart cluster round a low-pressure system.

clue.text: I am excluded from smarter gossip

indicators.note: excluded from means the letter I is removed from the longer word

parts.note: nattier means smarter or more neatly dressed
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is left out of chatter among well-dressed people.
explanation.definitionFit: To chat idly is to chatter, a synonym of gossip.

clue.text: Tests involved with oriental fly

indicators.note: involved means the letters of tests are tangled together

parts.note: E stands for east, so oriental

explanation.surface: Laboratory trials on an Eastern insect.
explanation.definitionFit: The African insect that transmits sleeping sickness is a biting fly.
